title: WeekModel refresh skips a changed date with the same day of month
finding: timerEvent compares only currentDateTime().date().day() with m_today.date().day(). Different full dates with the same day number therefore skip the refresh path.
candidate_trigger: Retain the model across a clock change or long suspension from November 2 to December 2. On the next timer event, both day numbers are 2 and populateModel is skipped even though the displayed week belongs to the old date.
expected: Refresh the seven displayed days whenever the full local calendar date changes, including month/year changes that retain the same day number.
evidence: Permanent QTest exercises the production update path extracted from timerEvent while preserving the original day-number predicate. Same-day-number next-month, next-year and backward-month rows fail (no model reset); six control scenarios pass. No system clock changed or Android suspension simulated.
impact: Potential stale weekday/date header until a later date change or model recreation. No shopping-list data loss or frequency is established.
reproduction_to_collect: Use a minimal deterministic date-control seam to initialize the actual WeekModel on one date and deliver its refresh trigger on another date with the same day number.
Verify observable model roles against the new seven-day sequence, with unchanged-date and ordinary next-day controls.
Do not change the computer clock or introduce a general clock framework solely for this test.
regression_gap: Closed: permanent production-model regression fails before and passes after; included in normal CTest verification.
possible_correction: Implemented full QDate equality and date-only state. timerEvent supplies QDate::currentDate to protected updateDate, also exposed by a test-only subclass; no clock provider or QML API added.
implementation_scope: Selected UI-019 fix and its permanent QTest/documentation only. Reset notifications and unused timer ID are unchanged.

regression.after: Final focused run: 11 passed, 0 failed. Full normal model suite: 75 records pass, including all nine date scenarios.
regression.scope: Production timer update method with controlled dates, seven name/number roles, reset notifications and repeated-date no-op. Real timer delivery and Android lifecycle are not simulated.

resolution.change: Store QDate and compare full dates. timerEvent reads current local date once and passes it to protected updateDate, which tests expose through a test-only subclass. Populate all seven dates from that same value; existing remove/reset notifications retained.
resolution.before: Preserved original day-number predicate after extracting the timer update path: three same-day-number month/year/backward cases fail, six controls pass (8 pass/3 fail including fixture records).
resolution.after: All nine scenarios and repeated-date no-op assertions pass (11 records including fixtures); seven day-name/number roles and reset counts checked.

verification.analyzer_notes: Initial test-only diagnostics addressed with ISO date fixture strings and normal QObject test-adapter metadata/parent constructor. Both test-unit analyzers repeated after rebuilding generated metadata; unchanged WeekModel clean results retained. No suppression or profile change.
verification.limits: Controlled-date production update path, not actual OS clock changes, timer delivery or Android suspension. Pure model fix; no new rendering/Android certification.

resolution.commit: Committed with this ticket's source changes and permanent regression tests; see Git history and DEV-006 closure.
